Dear Sirs, 
 
Sub:  Notice of 27th Annual General Meeting (AGM) and Integrated Annual Report of the 
Company for Financial Year 2025-26 (FY 2025-26). 
 
Ref:  
Compliance under Regulation 30 and 34 of Securities and Exchange Board of India 
(Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (the “Listing 
Regulations”) 
 
Kindly refer our letter dated 14th May 2026, regarding intimation of 27th AGM of the Company to be 
held on Tuesday, 4th August 2026 at 3:30 pm (Indian Standard Time), through Video Conferencing 
(VC)/ Other Audio-Visual Means (OAVM). 
 
In continuation of the aforesaid letter, we hereby enclose the following: 
 
a) Notice of the 27th AGM of the Company along with e-voting instructions and brief details of agenda 
items proposed to be transacted thereat (Annexure 1). 
 
b) Integrated Annual Report for FY 2025-26, including Business Responsibility and Sustainability 
Report. 
 
Aforesaid documents are being sent electronically to shareholders whose email addresses are registered 
with the Company/ Depository Participant. 
 
Further, in accordance with Regulation 36(1)(b) of the Listing Regulations, the Company is also sending 
a letter to those Members whose e-mail addresses are not registered with the Company/RTA/DPs, 
providing the weblink from where the Integrated Annual Report for the FY 2025-26 can be accessed 
on the Company’s website. 
 
 
 

                                
                                                                                                                                                 
  
                           
 
 
 
 
The Integrated Annual Report along with AGM Notice can also be accessed/ downloaded at 
https://www.diageoindia.com/integrated-annual-report-fy2025-26 
 
This is for your information and records. 
 
Thank you, 
 
For United Spirits Limited 
 
 
 
Pragya Kaul

NOTICE is hereby given that the 27th (twenty-seventh) Annual 
General Meeting (“AGM”) of members of United Spirits Limited (“the 
Company”/“USL”) will be held on Tuesday, 4th August 2026 at 3:30 
P.M. IST through Video Conferencing (“VC”)/Other Audio-Visual 
Means (“OAVM”) to transact the following businesses:
ORDINARY BUSINESS
1.	
To receive, consider and adopt Audited Standalone 
Financial Statements of the Company for the financial 
year ended 31st March 2026, and the reports of Board of 
Directors and Auditors thereon.
	
To consider and, if thought fit, to pass the following resolution as 
an Ordinary Resolution:
	
“RESOLVED THAT the Audited Standalone Financial Statements 
of the Company for the financial year ended 31st March 2026, 
and the reports of Board of Directors and Auditors thereon, as 
circulated to members, be considered and adopted.”
2. 	
To receive, consider and adopt Audited Consolidated 
Financial Statements of the Company for the financial 
year ended 31st March 2026, and the reports of Board of 
Directors and Auditors thereon.
	
To consider and, if thought fit, to pass the following resolution as 
an Ordinary Resolution:
	
“RESOLVED THAT the Audited Consolidated Financial Statements 
of the Company for the financial year ended 31st March 2026, 
and the reports of Board of Directors and Auditors thereon, as 
circulated to members, be considered and adopted.”
3.	
To declare final dividend of ` 11 per equity share for 
financial year ended 31st March 2026.
	
To consider and, if thought fit, to pass the following resolution as 
an Ordinary Resolution:
	
“RESOLVED THAT pursuant to recommendation of Board of 
Directors of the Company, a final dividend of ` 11 (550%) per 
equity share of face value of ` 2 per equity share for the financial 
year ended 31st March 2026, be and is hereby declared and paid 
out of profits of financial year 2025-26 to equity shareholders of 
the Company whose name appear in the Register of Members 
of the Company as on Wednesday, 8th July 2026.”
4.	
To appoint a Director in place of Mr. Pradeep Jain (DIN: 
02110401) who retires by rotation and being eligible, offers 
himself for re-appointment.
	
To consider and, if thought fit, to pass the following resolution as 
an Ordinary Resolution:

and Exchange Board of India (“SEBI”) (Listing Obligations 
and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (the “Listing 
Regulations”), and Secretarial Standard on General Meetings

Chartered Accountants as Statutory Auditors of the 
Company.
	
To consider and, if thought fit, to pass the following resolution as 
an Ordinary Resolution:
	
“RESOLVED THAT pursuant to the provisions of section 139, 142 
and all other applicable provisions, if any, of the Companies 
Act, 2013 and rules framed thereunder, the Securities and 
Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure 
Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (the “Listing Regulations”) 
(including any statutory modification(s) or re-enactment thereof 
for the time being in force) and upon recommendations of 
the Audit Committee and the Board of Directors, M/s. Walker 
Chandiok & Co LLP, Chartered Accountants (Firm Registration 
No. 001076N/N500013), be and are hereby appointed as the 
Statutory Auditors of the Company for a term of 5 (five) years 
i.e., from the conclusion of this Annual General Meeting till the 
conclusion of 32nd (thirty-second) Annual General Meeting of the 
Company, on such remuneration as may be recommended by 
the Audit Committee, in consultation with the Auditors and duly 
approved by the Board of Directors.
	
RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the Audit Committee/Board of 
Directors of the Company, be and are hereby authorized to 
revise/alter/modify/amend the terms and conditions and/or 
remuneration, from time to time, as may be mutually agreed with 
the Statutory Auditors, during the tenure of their appointment.
	
RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the Board be and is hereby authorised 
to do all acts, deeds, matters and things and take all such steps 
as may be necessary, proper or expedient to give effect to this 
resolution and to delegate all or any of its powers herein conferred 
to any Director, Company Secretary or any other officer(s) of the 
Company.”

Remuneration payable to M/s. Rao, Murthy & Associates, 
Cost Auditor of the Company for the financial year ending 
31st March 2027.
	
To consider and, if thought fit, to pass the following resolution as 
an Ordinary Resolution:
	
“RESOLVED THAT pursuant to provisions of section 148 and other 
applicable provisions, if any, of the Companies Act, 2013, read 
with the Companies (Audit and Auditors) Rules, 2014 (including 
any statutory modification(s) or re-enactment(s) thereof, for the

is hereby accorded for the proposed remuneration not exceeding 
` 2.25 Lakh plus out of pocket expenses and applicable taxes, 
payable to M/s. Rao, Murthy & Associates, Cost Accountants, 
(Firm Registration Number: 000065), appointed by the Board 
of Directors of the Company on the recommendation of Audit 
Committee, as Cost Auditor of the Company, to conduct cost 
audit of the Company for financial year 2026-27.
	
RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the Board be and is hereby authorised 
to do all acts, deeds, matters and things and take all such steps 
as may be necessary, proper or expedient to give effect to this 
resolution and to delegate all or any of its powers herein conferred 
to any Director, Company Secretary or any other officer(s) of the 
Company.”
7.	
Appointment of Mr. Vinod Rao (DIN: 01788921) as an 
Independent Director of the Company
	
To consider and, if thought fit, to pass the following resolution as 
a Special Resolution:
	
“RESOLVED THAT in accordance with the provisions of sections 
149, 150, 152, 161, Schedule IV and other applicable provisions, if 
any, of the Companies Act, 2013 and the Rules made thereunder 
and Regulation 17, 25 and other applicable provisions of the 
Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations 
and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (the “Listing 
Regulations”) (including any statutory modification(s) or re-
enactment(s) thereof for the time being in force), the Articles of 
Association of the Company, Mr. Vinod Rao (DIN: 01788921), who 
was appointed by the Board of Directors on the recommendation 
of Nomination and Remuneration Committee as an Additional 
Director (Non-Executive, Independent Director) with effect from 13th 
June 2026, and who meets the criteria for independence under 
section 149(6) of the Act and the Rules made thereunder and 
Regulation 16(1)(b) of the Listing Regulations, and has consented 
to act as a Director of the Company and in respect of whom the 
Company has received a notice in writing from a member under 
section 160 of the Act proposing his candidature for the office 
of Director of the Company, be and is hereby appointed as an 
Independent Director of the Company for a period of three years, 
effective from 13th June 2026 to 12th June 2029, and whose office 
shall not be liable to retire by rotation.
	
RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the Board be and is hereby authorised 
to do all acts, deeds, matters and things and take all such steps 
as may be necessary, proper or expedient to give effect to this 
resolution and to delegate all or any of its powers herein conferred 
to any Director, Company Secretary or any other officer(s) of the 
Company.” 
8.	
Appointment of Mr. Daniel Mobley (DIN: 11790849) as a 
Non-Executive Non-Independent Director of the Company
	
To consider and, if thought fit, to pass the following resolution as 
an Ordinary Resolution:
	
“RESOLVED THAT in accordance with the provisions of section 
149, 152, 161 of the Companies Act, 2013 and the Rules made 
thereunder and Regulation 17 of the Securities and Exchange 
Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) 
Regulations, 2015 (the “Listing Regulations”) (including any 
statutory modification(s) or reenactment( s) thereof for the time 
being in force), the Articles of Association of the Company, 
Mr. Daniel Mobley (DIN: 11790849), who was appointed by 
the Board of Directors on the recommendation of Nomination 
and Remuneration Committee as an Additional Director (Non-
Executive, Non-Independent Director) with effect from 6th July 
2026, and who is eligible for appointment and has consented 
to act as a Director of the Company and in respect of whom the 
Company has received a notice in writing from a member under 
section 160 of the Act proposing his candidature for the office of 
Director of the Company, be and is hereby appointed as Non-
Executive Non-Independent Director, liable to retire by rotation.  
	
RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the Board be and is hereby authorised 
to do all acts, deeds, matters and things and take all such steps 
as may be necessary, proper or expedient to give effect to this 
resolution and to delegate all or any of its powers herein conferred 
to any Director, Company Secretary or any other officer(s) of the 
Company.”

NOTES
Virtual Meeting:
1.	
The Ministry of Corporate Affairs (“MCA”) vide its General Circular 
No. 20/2020 dated 5th May 2020 read with subsequent circulars 
issued from time to time, the latest one being General Circular 
No. 03/2025 dated 22nd September 2025, (“MCA Circulars”) 
and Securities and Exchange Board of India (“SEBI”) vide its 
Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/CMD1/CIR/P/2020/79 dated 12th 
May 2020 read with subsequent circulars issued from time to 
time, the latest one being Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-
2/P/CIR/2024/133 dated 3rd October 2024, (“SEBI Circulars”) 
(hereinafter collectively referred to as “Circulars”) has permitted 
companies to conduct AGM through Video Conferencing or 
Other Audio Visual Means (“VC/OAVM”), without physical 
presence of members at a common venue, until further orders. 
Accordingly, in compliance with the provisions of the Companies 
Act, 2013 (“Act”) SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure 
Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (“SEBI Listing Regulations”) and 
above Circulars, 27th (twenty-seventh) AGM of the Company is 
being held through VC/OAVM on Tuesday, 4th August 2026 at 
3.30 P.M. IST with deemed venue being the Registered Office of 
the Company.
2.	
Members to note that National Securities Depository Limited 
(“NSDL”) will be providing facilities of voting through remote 
electronic voting (“e-voting”) and e-voting during the AGM. 
VCNow will facilitate the participation in AGM through VC/
OAVM. The procedure for participating in the meeting through 
VC/OAVM is explained in detail in Annexure 2 and is also 
available on the Company’s website at www.diageoindia.com.
3.	
Participation of members through VC/OAVM will be reckoned for 
the purpose of quorum for the AGM as per section 103 of the Act.
4.	
Pursuant to Regulation 44 of SEBI Listing Regulations and the 
aforesaid circulars, facility for appointment of Proxy by members 
is not available for this AGM. Accordingly, proxy form, attendance 
slip including route map to the venue are not annexed to 
this Notice.
	
However, pursuant to section 112 and 113 of the Act, representatives 
of members such as the President of India or the Governor of a 
State or body corporate can attend this AGM through VC/OAVM 
and cast their votes through e-voting.
Authorized Representative:
5.	
Institutional/Corporate members intending to authorize its 
representatives to participate and/or vote at the AGM through 
VC/OAVM are requested to send a scanned copy (PDF/JPEG) 
of the certified copy of Board Resolution/Authorization Letter, 
authorizing its representatives to the Scrutinizer by email at sudhir.
compsec@gmail.com or to the Company at investor.india@
diageo.com or upload the same on VC portal/e-voting portal.
Electronic dispatch of Integrated Annual Report and process for 
registration of e-mail ID and for obtaining copy of Integrated 
Annual Report:
6.	
In compliance with aforesaid Circulars and Regulation 36(1)
(a) of SEBI Listing Regulations, the 27th (twenty-seventh) AGM 
Notice along with Integrated Annual Report for Financial Year 
2025-26 (FY 2025-26) is being sent through electronic mode to 
those members whose email addresses are registered with the 
Company/Depositories/Registrar and Transfer Agent (RTA) as on 
Wednesday, 8th July 2026. Further, in compliance with Regulation 
36(1)(b) of the Listing Regulations, a letter providing the web-
link, including the exact path, where Integrated Annual Report 
for the FY 2025-26 is available, is being sent to those members 
whose e-mail address is not registered with the Company/RTA/
Depository Participants (“DP”).
7.	
Members may note that the AGM Notice and Integrated Annual 
Report for FY 2025-26 is also available on the Company’s 
website at www.diageoindia.com, websites of Stock Exchanges 
viz., the BSE Limited (“BSE”) and the National Stock Exchange of 
India Limited (“NSE”) at www.bseindia.com and www.nseindia.
com, respectively.
8.	
Members are required to immediately inform details of their 
email addresses, if any, as mentioned below, in order to receive 
all notices and other statutory documents which are required to 
be sent to members of the Company as per the Act and the 
Listing Regulations:
	
a)	
In case of shares held in physical form – to the Company’s 
RTA viz., Integrated Registry Management Services Private 
Limited at #30, Ramana Residency, 4th Cross, Sampige 
Road, Bengaluru – 560 003, Karnataka, India. (Tel No. 
+91 80 2346 0815-818 Fax No. +91 80 2346 0819), and
	
b)	
In case of shares held in dematerialized/electronic form – 
to respective DP.
9.	
Physical copy of Integrated Annual Report for FY 2025-26 
(including 27th AGM Notice) shall be sent only to those members 
who specifically request for the same. Accordingly, members 
who wish to obtain a physical copy of the above, may write to 
the Company at investor.india@diageo.com or to the RTA at 
bglsta@integratedindia.in, requesting the same, by providing 
their holding details.
Members holding shares in physical mode (“Physical 
members”):
10.	
Physical members to note that effective 1st April 2019, transfer 
of shares through physical mode are not permitted pursuant to 
SEBI notification dated 8th June 2018. Additionally, the Company’s 
equity shares are under compulsory dematerialization viz., trading 
of these shares would be facilitated through stock exchanges only 
if physical shares are dematerialized.

a demat account with an authorised DP and arrange for 
dematerializing their physical shareholding in the Company.

Members are requested to use this opportunity and reach out to

11.	
Physical members to note that SEBI vide its Master Circular No. 
SEBI/HO/38/13/(4)2026-MIRSD-POD/I/4298/2026 dated 6th 
February 2026 (“SEBI Master Circular”) has mandated listed 
companies to issue securities only in demat form while processing 
service requests viz., issuance of duplicate securities certificate, 
claim from unclaimed suspense account, renewal/exchange 
of securities certificate, endorsement, sub-division/splitting of 
securities certificate, consolidation of securities certificates/folios, 
transmission or transposition.
	
Accordingly, members are requested to make service requests 
by submitting a duly filled and signed Form ISR-4, format of 
which is made available on Company’s website at https://www.
diageoindia.com/en/investors/shareholder-centre/downloads. 
Additionally, all service requests shall be processed only after the 
folio is KYC Compliant.
12.	
Physical members have been mandated to furnish PAN, choice 
of Nomination (optional), contact details, bank account details 
and specimen signature for their corresponding folio numbers 
vide SEBI Master Circular.
	
Accordingly, Physical members are requested to submit duly 
filled and signed prescribed forms by sending an email from 
their registered email ID to bglsta@integratedindia.in and send 
physical copies of the above to Integrated Registry Management 
Service Private Limited, Unit: United Spirits, Limited, No. 30, 
Ramana Residency, 4th Cross, Sampige Road, Malleswaram, 
Bengaluru – 560 003, Karnataka, India.
	
Format of prescribed forms are made available on Company’s 
website at https://www.diageoindia.com/en/investors/
shareholder-centre/downloads.
13.	
Effective 1st April 2024, Physical members whose folios are not 
updated with any of aforesaid KYC details, shall be eligible to 
get dividend in electronic mode, only after furnishing their KYC 
details. Accordingly, the Company encourages physical members 
to ensure their folios are KYC compliant in order to receive their 
dividends in a timely manner. 
Dividends and related matters:
14.	
The Board of Directors of the Company at their meeting held 
on 14th May 2026, has inter alia, approved and recommended 
payment of final dividend of `11 (Rupees Eleven only) per equity 
share of face value of `2 (Rupees Two only) each, for FY 2025-26, 
subject to approval of members at this AGM.
15.	
Final dividend for FY 2025-26, if approved by members at the 
ensuing AGM, will be paid on or after Thursday , 13th August 
2026, to those members whose names appear on the Register 
of Members of the Company or Register of Beneficial Owners 
maintained by the Depositories as on the record date i.e., 
Wednesday, 8th July 2026.
16.	
Members holding shares in physical/demat form are hereby 
informed that bank particulars registered with RTA or their 
respective DP, as the case may be, will be considered by the 
Company for payment of final dividend. Accordingly, members 
are required to submit their bank account details, if not already 
registered, as mandated by the SEBI.
	
Further, members are requested to ensure that their PAN is linked 
to Aadhaar as per the date specified by the Central Board of 
Direct Taxes.
	
FAQs on Tax deducted at Source on Dividend are available on 
the website of the Company at https://www.diageoindia.com/
en/investors/shareholder-centre/downloads

Pursuant to provisions of the IEPF Authority (Accounting, Audit,

has uploaded details of unpaid and unclaimed amounts lying 
with the Company as on 31st March 2026 on Company’s website

20.	
During FY 2025-26, the Company transferred ` 5.3 crore to IEPF 
towards the Interim and Final dividend of FY 2024-25 and Interim

Members may note that unclaimed dividends which are

Tax on Dividends:
22.	
As per the Income Tax Act, 2025, dividends paid or distributed 
by the Company after 1st April 2020, shall be taxable in the hands 
of members and the Company shall be required to deduct tax 
at source (“TDS”) at prescribed rates from dividend to be paid to 
such members. For prescribed rates for various categories, kindly 
refer to the Income Tax Act, 2025 and amendments thereof.
	
a.	
An email communication was sent to all members informing 
relevant procedure to be adopted by them/documents to 
be submitted for availing applicable tax rate.
	
b.	
Resident and Non-Resident members are requested to duly 
fill and sign aforesaid documents and upload the same, 
as applicable, only on RTA’s weblink i.e., https://ipostatus.
integratedregistry.in/TaxExemptionRegistration.aspx on or 
before Wednesday, 15th July 2026, , to enable the Company 
to determine appropriate TDS/withholding tax rate for the 
proposed final dividend for FY 2025-26. Further members 
may note that tax determination/deduction received post 
Wednesday, 15th July 2026, shall not be considered for 
payment of final dividend for FY 2025-26. For any queries/
clarification, members may address the same to bglsta@
integratedindia.in.
	
c.	
Members to note that in case tax on aforesaid dividend 
is deducted at a higher rate due to non-receipt of or 
satisfactory completeness of the aforementioned details/
documents by Wednesday, 15th July 2026, members may 
claim an appropriate refund in their return of income filed 
with respective tax authorities.
	
d.	
Members are requested to ensure that their PAN, choice 
of nomination, contact details including mobile number, 
email ID, bank account details and residential status of their 
demat accounts are updated with DP, in order to receive 
communications from the Company and any benefits 
arising out of corporate action in a timely manner. Any 
change in aforesaid details is required to updated with your 
DP directly.
	
e.	
No tax will be deducted at source, in the case of resident 
individual members where the aggregate dividend payable 
during the financial year does not exceed ` 10,000. 
However, where the PAN is not updated in the records of 
the Company, its Registrar and RTA or the DP, or where

Item No. 5
Appointment of M/s. Walker Chandiok & Co. LLP, Chartered 
Accountants as Statutory Auditors of the Company.
The Members of the Company at the 22nd AGM held on 26th August 
2021 had approved the re-appointment of M/s. Price Waterhouse & 
Co Chartered Accountants LLP, (FRN 304026E/E-300009), as the 
Statutory Auditors of the Company to hold office for a term of 5 (five) 
consecutive years from the conclusion of said AGM till the conclusion 
of the 27th AGM. They will complete their two consecutive terms as 
Statutory Auditors of the Company on conclusion of this AGM.
The Board of Directors of the Company (the “Board”), at their meeting 
held on 21st November 2025, considering the experience, expertise and 
based on the recommendation of the Audit Committee, has proposed 
the appointment of M/s. Walker Chandiok & Co. LLP, Chartered 
Accountants (Firm Registration No. 001076N/N500013), as Statutory 
Auditors of the Company, to the Members of the Company.
A robust process was followed for shortlisting of statutory audit firm 
commencing with a Request for Proposal (RFP) to large audit firms. 
Based on subsequent interactions, few firms opted out of the process 
citing non-audit services being rendered to Diageo group. The remaining 
shortlisted firms made a formal presentation to the Independent 
Directors of the Audit Committee followed by an interaction. After 
evaluating the proposals and considering all relevant factors including 
audit quality management initiatives, technology deployment, audit 
team, profile of the proposed engagement partner, industry experience, 
client pedigree amongst others, M/s. Walker Chandiok & Co. LLP has 
been recommended for appointment. Audit Committee was periodically 
apprised of the process.
The proposed appointment is for a term of 5 (five) consecutive years 
from the conclusion of 27th AGM till the conclusion of the 32nd AGM 
on payment of such remuneration as may be mutually agreed upon 
between the Board of Directors and the Statutory Auditors, from time 
to time
The proposed remuneration to be paid to the Statutory Auditors for the 
financial year 2026-27 is ` 259 lakhs (Rupees Two Hundred Fifty-Nine 
Lakhs Only), comprising the statutory audit fee, limited review fee and 
BRSR reasonable assurance fee, in addition, certification fees shall be 
payable at ` 1 lakh (Rupees One Lakh Only) per certification for other 
permissible services, plus reimbursement of out-of-pocket expenses and 
applicable taxes. Besides the aforesaid services, the Company would 
also obtain other permissible non-audit services from the statutory 
auditors under various statutory regulations as required from time to 
time, for which they will be remunerated separately on mutually agreed 
terms, as approved by the Board of Directors in consultation with the 
Audit Committee. The fees, if any, for the permitted non-audit services 
shall not exceed 20% of the annual audit fees. 
The remuneration for the remaining period of the term shall be fixed 
by the Board of Directors based on the recommendation of the Audit 
Committee. The proposed remuneration is commensurate with the size 
of the Company as per the nature of its business and is determined 
based on the recommendation of the Audit Committee, which peruses 
the industry benchmarks, profile of the firm, scope of audit and other 
relevant factors. The Company shall not avail any services from the 
Statutory Auditors which are prohibited under section 144 of the Act.
The proposed fees payable to M/s. Walker Chandiok & Co. LLP is 
lower than the fee paid to the outgoing statutory auditor. The reduction 
is attributable to the incoming auditor’s proposed engagement and 
resource model, technology-enabled audit approach, efficiencies 
identified during the audit transition process, pre-emptive discussion 
of significant accounting matters and is in line with the peer group 
benchmarking. The Audit Committee has evaluated the auditor’s 
qualifications, experience, independence, audit scope and fee structure 
and is satisfied that the proposed remuneration is reasonable and 
commensurate with the scope and complexity of the audit engagement.
M/s. Walker Chandiok & Co. LLP is a firm of Chartered Accountants 
registered and empanelled with the Institute of Chartered Accountants 
of India (“ICAI”). It was established in the year 1935 and is a Limited 
Liability Partnership Firm incorporated in India. It has its registered 
office at L-41, Connaught Circus, New Delhi - 110001 apart from 15 
other branch offices in various cities in India. It is primarily engaged 
in providing audit and assurance services to its clients. It is amongst 
the largest and highly reputed audit firms in India and are auditors for 
several large companies including some of the top 100 listed entities 
in India.
Pursuant to section 139 of the Act and the Rules framed thereunder, the 
Company has received written consent from M/s. Walker Chandiok & 
Co. LLP and a certificate that they satisfy the criteria provided under 
section 141 of the Act and that the appointment, if made, shall be in 
accordance with the applicable provisions of the Act and Rules framed 
thereunder. As required under the Listing Regulations, M/s. Walker 
Chandiok & Co. LLP, has confirmed that they hold a valid certificate 
issued by the Peer Review Board of the ICAI.

About the Report
This is the second Integrated Annual Report of United Spirits Limited (USL), also referred to as Diageo 
India or the Company. This Report presents a balanced view of our financial and non-financial 
performance, while explaining how we conduct our business, create value and deliver outcomes for 
our stakeholders, not limited to statutory requirements. It also provides insights into our business model, 
material matters, risks and opportunities, strategic priorities, governance practices, performance and 
outlook. Through these integrated disclosures, we aim to provide providers of financial capital and 
other stakeholders with relevant information to support informed decision-making.
Reporting Period  
and Scope
All financial and non-financial information presented in this 
Report pertains to USL, unless otherwise stated, for the period 
from April 1, 2025 to March 31, 2026. Wherever relevant, we 
have included historical trends for key performance indicators, 
including ESG metrics, to help readers understand our 
value-creation journey more comprehensively.
Reporting Framework, 
Guidelines and 
Standards
The Report should be read together with the annual accounts for a 
complete understanding of our financial performance.
•	The narrative section of the Report follows the principles of 
the International Integrated Reporting Council’s Framework, 
overseen by the IFRS Foundation. 
•	The statutory sections of the Report comply with, report 
on or reference applicable requirements and frameworks. 
These sections include:
	» Board’s Report
	» Management Discussion and Analysis
	» Corporate Governance Report
	» Business Responsibility and Sustainability Reporting
	» Financial Statements
•	The applicable requirements and frameworks include:
	» Companies Act, 2013 and its associated rules
	» Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations 
and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015
	» Revised Secretarial Standards issued by The Institute of 
Company Secretaries of India
	» Indian Accounting Standards
	» National Guidelines on Responsible Business Conduct
	» United Nations Sustainable Development Goals

and raise, which are prudently deployed across

consumer-first mindset of our people. We invest 
in their development and foster an equitable,

trust and enduring relationships we have built

to our operations, including water, energy and

consumer trust and emotional connection in the 
market. Our innovative, premium portfolio and

manufacturing, logistics and sales capabilities, 
and supports our digital transformation into a 
future-ready organisation.

Chairperson’s 
Message
Against this backdrop, India continued to 
distinguish itself as one of the world's most 
resilient and attractive growth markets. 
Strong domestic demand, a young and 
aspirational consumer base, improving 
infrastructure, and growing strategic 
relevance in global trade have reinforced 
confidence in the country's long-term 
prospects.
It is within this context that United Spirits 
Limited (Diageo India) delivered another 
year of impressive performance and 
strategic progress. This was my first full 
year as Chairperson of the Company, and 
it has reinforced my conviction that we are 
exceptionally well positioned to benefit 
from the opportunities that lie ahead. 
FY 2025-26 was also the first full year 
under Praveen Someshwar's leadership 
as Managing Director and Chief Executive 
Officer. The continuity of strategic direction 
that he has brought, combined with fresh 
energy, a clear consumer-first mindset, 
and disciplined execution, gives the Board 
considerable confidence as we enter the 
next phase of growth.
Long-term value creation requires not 
only building exceptional assets but also 
allocating capital where it can generate 
the greatest strategic and financial returns. 
The Board believes this decision serves the 
long-term interests of all stakeholders.
Navigating a Changing 
Environment
The Board remains clear-eyed about both 
the challenges and opportunities that lie 
ahead.
Tensions in West Asia have disrupted 
shipping routes and contributed to 
higher logistic and packaging material 
costs during the latter part of the year. 
Volatility in crude oil prices created 
additional pressure on packaging inputs, 
while shifting trade policies and currency 
movements introduced uncertainty across 
global markets.
While these factors represent near-term 
headwinds, they also reinforce the 
importance of resilience, agility, and 
disciplined execution. The Board is 
encouraged by the actions management 
is taking to mitigate these pressures 
through productivity initiatives, supply 
chain optimisation, and constructive 
engagement with state authorities.
At the same time, periods of global 
disruption often reinforce structural 
advantages. India's growing importance 
as both a manufacturing hub and 
consumption market, its expanding 
network of trade relationships, and the 
resilience of its domestic demand story 
have become increasingly evident in the 
current environment.
In this context, the signing of the India-UK 
Free Trade Agreement is a development 
the Board views with considerable 
optimism. For India, the world's largest 
whisky market, the agreement has 
the potential to be transformative. 
Reduced tariffs on Scotch whisky will 
improve accessibility for consumers, 
support premiumisation within the 
category, and generate meaningful 
long-term cost benefits through lower 
import duties on bulk Scotch.
Building a Future-Ready 
Organisation
Sustaining growth over the coming 
decade will require more than a strong 
portfolio. It will require an organisation 
that can adapt quickly, harness 
technology effectively, and attract and 
develop exceptional talent.
The Board is encouraged by the progress 
management has made in embedding 
AI and advanced analytics across the 
business. These capabilities are enhancing 
decision-making, improving agility, 
and creating meaningful operational 
advantages across commercial and 
supply chain functions.
Equally important is the Company's 
culture. Strong employee engagement 
scores and external recognition for 
inclusion and workplace excellence reflect

significant excise policy frameworks

Madhya Pradesh all continued to 
progress. The structural drivers shaping 
India's consumption story are intact, 
and the anticipated India-UK Free Trade 
Agreement, adds a further meaningful 
tailwind.
Strengthening Our Portfolio
India is not one consumer market. It is 
three. A vast aspirational base seeking 
affordable access to better quality. 
A growing middle class premiumising 
with confidence. And an affluent segment 
demanding luxury experiences and 
repertoire variety. Our portfolio is built to 
serve all three, across BII and BIO whisky, 
white spirits, and Indian single malts, with 
differentiated strategies for each.

Challenge grew ahead of the category, 
with the 180ml pocket pack delivering 
double-digit growth and expanding

work, we have also launched the most

this transformed bundle has launched in

through its Savour the Pause renovation

Walker strengthened its luxury credentials

to ` 1,000 Crores in NSV over the next 18

behind future growth opportunities.

creators, consumers, and communities

craftsmanship in spirits.

doing business responsibly. During the 
year, we continued to advance our 
sustainability agenda through water 
stewardship initiatives under The Godavari

skilling initiatives through Learning for Life.

must be both inclusive and sustainable

consumers are increasing their repertoire, choosing different 
drinks for different occasions.

We have embedded a strong food safety and quality culture across all levels of the organisation to ensure consistent product integrity and enhance 
customer and consumer satisfaction. Our approach is anchored in three key pillars:
Rigorous Standards and Process 
Excellence
We mitigate quality risks and safeguard consumers 
through processes aligned with Global Risk Management 
Standards (GRMS) and FSSAI regulations, including a 
structured product recall mechanism. Oversight is provided 
by central and site-level steering committees, supported by 
a Crisis Management Team (CMT) chaired by the MD and 
CEO. Annual mock recalls are conducted to strengthen 
emergency preparedness.
All products undergo stringent quality checks, including 
hourly inspections across packaging lines supported by a 
positive release mechanism. We also monitor distribution 
quality at the first point of sale to assess product integrity 
during transit and drive improvements. Additionally, annual 
third-party on-shelf assessments are conducted based 
on Consumer Relevant Quality Standards (CRQS), along 
with competitor benchmarking. These insights and quality 
KPIs are continuously tracked to ensure consistent product 
delivery and reinforce consumer confidence.
Cross-functional Collaboration

alignment on quality goals across the organisation.
Building Quality Capabilities

We have a qualified and capable team of food safety 
and quality professionals overseeing quality control 
and assurance across the value chain. New joiners 
undergo comprehensive induction and refresher training, 
including sensory and on-the-job training modules.
Capability-building initiatives include weekly ‘Gurukul’ 
training sessions covering quality standards, global 
practices, and internal SOPs for manufacturing 
teams, as well as the ‘RISE Together’ programme for 
cross-functional learning at supplier locations. We also 
participate in external certifications, awards, and 
platforms such as CII, ICQC, and RBNQA to gain an 
external perspective and drive continuous improvement.
We have established Centres of Excellence in liquid and 
packaging quality, supported by specialised external 
training and certification programmes.

Supply Chain and Distribution 
Excellence

operational agility.

strengthening supply chain resilience. These include:

services, materials and meet timelines in a compliant 
manner.

sustainability questionnaires aligned with our ESG 
action plan in vendor contracts, along with securing 
contractual commitments from high-impact suppliers.

Safety performance is monitored through a balanced focus 
on leading and lagging indicators, supported by structured 
reporting through Safety Improvement Report Cards

Formal hazard identification and risk assessment processes 
are carried out across activities, with gaps addressed through 
corrective actions and residual risks reviewed after controls 
are implemented. Regular training strengthens capabilities 
to identify risks, investigate incidents, and apply learnings 
consistently in day-to-day operations. Incident learnings 
are shared across the organisation to strengthen preventive 
measures and support broader deployment of effective 
controls.
Safety Communication, Engagement and 
Continual Improvement
Governance: EHS performance is sustained through 
disciplined governance, clear communication, and workforce 
engagement. Daily Tier 1 shopfloor reviews under the 
SQDCMS framework ensure safety remains a priority and 
enable immediate escalation of concerns. Performance is 
further reviewed at Department Head and Unit Management 
levels. Each unit operates a Central Safety Committee, with 
equal representation from workers and management and 
chaired by the Unit Head, to review KPIs, resolve issues, and 
track actions to closure.
Communication: Clear and consistent communication 
reinforces EHS priorities across the organisation. This includes 
monthly safety campaigns focused on SFIP standards, town 
halls, and targeted as well as organisation-wide training 
programmes. 
Continual improvement: Continual improvement is driven 
through Kaizen, One Page Learning, Safety Action Meetings, 
and Focused Improvement projects using the DMAIC 
framework, alongside Yellow and Green Belt initiatives. 
Safety Improvement Report Cards further support structured 
identification, prioritisation, and closure of unsafe conditions.
Health and Safety Initiatives 
During the year, the Company strengthened its safety agenda 
by focusing on high risk areas and advancing system-led 
improvements that embed prevention into daily operations. 
The overall effort centred on stronger process discipline, 
wider digital adoption, and sharper risk visibility across sites. 
This approach improved assurance, standardised critical 
workflows, and supported timely closure of actions while 
reinforcing safety as a consistent operating priority.
Digitisation
Digitisation of core safety processes strengthened compliance, 
traceability, and response effectiveness. This includes 
digitisation of the Work Permit System under Control of Work, 
the Safety Management System covering safety observations, 
automated CAPA and audit management, and Management 
of Change. The Company has already deployed Digitised 
Work Permit System, Management of Changed (MOC) and 
now have initiated deployment of an EHS Portal as a single 
system of record, with a phased eight module rollout planned 
over approximately 16 months covering Behaviour-Based 
Safety, EHS Audits, Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment 
(HIRA), Hazard and Operability Study (HAZOP), and Aspect–
Impact management.
Road safety governance for business driving was strengthened 
through deployment of the Autobeacon mobile application, 
which uses smartphone-based indicators such as over 
speeding, harsh braking, rapid acceleration, and distracted 
driving to generate trip-level Safe Driving Scores and enable 
timely coaching and corrective actions.

evaluating risk profile (based on country risks, supplier spends and 
key input materials), operational and strategic importance, and 
their alignment with our ‘Spirit of Progress’ and the Responsible 
Sourcing framework. The process encompasses standardised 
selection templates and sustainability questionnaires on parameters 
like labour standards, human rights (including child and forced 
labour), environmental performance and legal compliance. 
These elements are integrated into all contracts and bidding 
processes, with contractual obligations for all suppliers.
For all high-risk supplier partners enhanced due diligence is 
mandated. High Risk Suppliers are evaluated basis country 
risks, supplier spends and key input materials. They must register 
with SEDEX and complete its Self-Assessment Questionnaire 
(SAQ), aligned with our Responsible Sourcing programme. 
High-risk suppliers are also required to undergo independent audits 
as per the SMETA four-pillar audit protocol or its equivalent. This is 
monitored and reviewed monthly and necessary actions are taken 
on need basis.
We believe that early awareness of potential breaches enables 
us to respond swiftly and effectively. Every report is treated with 
the utmost seriousness, and we firmly uphold a zero-tolerance 
policy against any retaliation from a Diageo employee towards 
suppliers or agency partners who raise concerns in good faith or 
assist with investigations. We encourage our suppliers and agency 
partners to share any issues regarding our business practices, or 
possible violations of our Standard or Code of Business Conduct, 
directly with their Diageo contact. Alternatively, concerns may be 
submitted through our SpeakUp service – a confidential platform 
available to employees and third parties (including suppliers), 
operated independently by an external company. SpeakUp offers 
trained staff who can support callers in their local languages, and is 
accessible via telephone, email, or internet, 24 hours a day, 7 days 
a week.

Ensuring Responsible Business Conduct
Code of Conduct
At Diageo India, the Code of Business Conduct guides employees in upholding ethical behaviour, integrity, 
and organisational values. It aligns with the global policies of the principal shareholder, Diageo plc, and 
sets out standards and guidelines across key areas of work. All employees complete a mandatory annual 
e-learning module as part of the Company’s compliance certification programme. New joiners are required to 
complete this training within 30 days of joining.
Anti-Corruption and Anti-Bribery
Diageo India maintains a zero-tolerance approach to corruption and bribery. The Company follows a 
comprehensive global anti-corruption policy established by its principal shareholder, Diageo plc, which 
addresses all forms of bribery and corruption. The core elements of this policy are embedded within the Code 
of Business Conduct and apply across all operations, including subsidiaries and value chain partners.
Whistle-blower Mechanism
Employees and value chain partners are encouraged to report any actual or suspected breaches of the Code 
of Conduct or Company policies through the confidential ‘Speak Up’ channel, managed by an independent 
external party. This channel is accessible via telephone, email, website, and QR code. Employees may also 
raise concerns through internal channels, including Business Integrity members, and the Human Resources 
and Legal departments, with assurance of protection from retaliation.
Respect for human rights remains integral to how we operate. 
Our approach is guided by Diageo plc’s Global Human Rights 
Policy, aligned with internationally recognised human rights 
charters. This policy reinforces our commitment to protecting and 
promoting the rights of all stakeholders, including employees, supply 
chain workers and partners, consumers, and communities where 
we operate. Our Dignity at Work policy, aligned with local laws and 
cultural norms, defines clear standards for personal integrity and 
conduct. These expectations extend to our suppliers through the 
Partnering with Suppliers Standard.
An annual legal compliance risk assessment is conducted under 
the supervision of the Risk Management Committee, covering 
areas such as human rights, bribery, and corruption. Human rights 
remain a key focus within the SEDEX Members Ethical Trade Audit 
(SMETA) four-pillar audits for high-risk suppliers, in line with Supplier 
Ethical Data Exchange (Sedex) protocols, as part of our responsible 
sourcing programme. Our Human Rights Impact Assessments 
(HRIAs) identify salient risks and vulnerable stakeholders across 
both our operations and supply chain.

10. Vigil Mechanism
 
 The Company has established whistle-blower mechanism 
known as ‘SpeakUp’, which is being independently operated 
by an independent agency. We encourage our employees or 
representatives acting on behalf of the Company, to raise the 
concerns through this mechanism, apart from other internal 
reporting channels viz. Line Manager, HR Business Partner, Legal 
Business Partner and Business Integrity partner.
 
 The SpeakUp channel is available on the Company’s website 
at https://www.diageoindia.com/en/about-us/corporate-
governance/speak-up with services available in English and 
5 other regional languages, and compliance concerns can 
be raised by any aggrieved person through web page or toll-
free number.
 
 The quality of investigation reports and remedial actions are 
reviewed and monitored by the Global Business Integrity team 
and the Company’s Business Integrity team. The decision 
on sanctions on the reported breaches are determined and 
monitored by a Compliance Committee for signiﬁcant breaches 
and the Grievance Committee for other breaches and people 
issues, ensuring there is a collective, transparent and unbiased 
decision-making process and that consistent action is undertaken 
in a timely manner to resolve the identiﬁed breaches.
 
 A structured Breach Management Standard is in place which 
is in line with the Global Standard, for timely and conclusive 
resolution of compliance concerns raised through the whistle 
blower mechanism.
 
 This vigil mechanism has been established to provide adequate 
safeguards against the victimization of employees, who avail 
this mechanism for reporting complaints and grievances in good 
faith and without fear of being punished for doing so. Access to 
the Chairperson of the Audit Committee is provided as required 
under the Act and the Listing Regulations.
11. 
Related party transactions
 
 The Company has adopted the Policy on dealing with Related 
Party Transactions (RPTs) in compliance with the requirements of 
the Act and Listing Regulations, as amended from time to time, 
which is available on the website of the Company at https://www.
diageoindia.com/policies/policyonrelatedpartytransactions. 
During the year under review, the said policy was amended to 
align with the amendments in Listing Regulations.
 
 The Policy aims to ensure that eﬀective procedures for reporting, 
approval, and other disclosures are established to govern 
transactions between the Company and Related Parties. The 
Policy focusses on the review and approval of Material RPTs, while 
addressing the potential or actual conﬂicts of interest that may 
arise out of these transactions. 
 
 All RPTs are placed before the Audit Committee and Board for 
review, recommendation and approval, as applicable. For RPTs 
of a repetitive nature or those undertaken in the ordinary course 
of business and at arm’s length, prior omnibus approval from 
the Audit Committee is obtained. Further, the Audit Committee 
on quarterly basis, reviews the details of the RPTs entered into by 
the Company pursuant to such omnibus approval. The Policy 
ensures compliance with regulatory guidelines and promotes 
accountability while adhering to the corporate governance 
principles. The Company continued to strengthen the RPT 
governance with the support of independent assessments by 
external professionals to ensure RPTs are in line with evolving 
regulations and governance practices.

 all RPTs were entered in ordinary course of business and on

 there are no materially signiﬁcant related party transactions

Risk Management
We deﬁne risk as “an uncertainty that could help or hinder achieving our business objectives”. We believe that eﬀective risk management starts 
with the right conversations to drive better business decisions. Our primary focus is to identify and embed mitigating actions for material risks that 
could impact our current or future performance, and/or our reputation. Our approach is structured to ensure that we take all reasonable steps to 
mitigate, but not necessarily eliminate, all risks in this context.
Risk Governance Framework
We have established a robust governance model designed to embed a riskaware culture throughout the organization. Each function holds ownership 
for identifying and reporting risks to the appropriate leadership tier, while the Governance function provides independent oversight and ensures 
alignment at the enterprise level.
Key pillars of our Risk Management Framework include:
• 
Three-Tier Risk Management Committee (RMC):
 
 A structured, multi-level committee system operating at the Functional, Executive, and Board levels to ensure comprehensive risk oversight 
and accountability.
• 
Well-Deﬁned Risk Management Policy:
 
A formal policy framework deﬁning risk governance, roles, responsibilities, and the end-to-end risk management process.
• 
Periodic Risk Review Meetings:
 
Periodic RMC meetings to assess the risk landscape, monitor mitigation progress, and evaluate emerging risks.
• 
Structured Risk Documentation:
 
 All critical risks are formally documented, with identiﬁed root causes, impact assessments, ownership accountability, and detailed, timebound 
mitigation plans with measurable indicators.
• 
Ongoing Monitoring & Dynamic Updates:
 
Risks are continuously tracked, with timely updates to risk proﬁles and mitigation actions to reﬂect changing business contexts.
• 
End-to-End Risk Coverage:
 
 The framework encompasses a wide range of strategic, ﬁnancial, operational, compliance, and emerging risks, both internal and external, 
ensuring holistic risk oversight.
Refer to the Risk Management section for further details.

Aﬀorestation, Alwar, 
Rajasthan
The project was initiated in partnership with the district forest Department, Alwar, Rajasthan where USL had 
planted 200K+ saplings under the project TOFI (Tree Outside forest in Rajasthan) at 19 diﬀerent locations. 
The plantation was maintained by USL for next 2 years.
Assessment Framework:
The assessment follows EIA frameworks adapted for tropical and semi-arid aﬀorestation, incorporating IPCC 
LULUCF carbon accounting guidelines, species-speciﬁc allometric equations (AGB = a × GBH × Height, 
47% C fraction), and GRI Standards 304 (Biodiversity) and 413 (Local Communities).
Objective: To increase Green Cover and biodiversity to establish a thriving, self-sustaining ecological system.
Output: 2,03,655 Saplings Planted and maintained with 26 species across 199.28 hectares.
Impact:
• 
 A weighted average survival rate of ~78% — signiﬁcantly above the national dryland aﬀorestation 
benchmark of 60–70% — conﬁrms strong ecological establishment.
• 
Ten of 19 sites recorded survival rates of 80% or above.
• 
 Natural regeneration of Khejri (Prosopis cineraria), the Rajasthan State Tree, was documented at Salpur, 
signaling positive ecological succession.
• 
Direct employment was generated at 9 of 19 sites.
• 
 The plantation is building a durable carbon sink projected to sequester 15,000–30,000 tones CO₂ 
equivalent per annum at maturity.
Wrong Side of the Road 
(WSOTR): Creating 
awareness on Impacts of 
drink driving:
Diageo India is implementing its programme on educating consumers on the impacts of drink driving. It is 
being implemented across various Regional Transport Oﬃces in India through a WSOTR Tab Lab model 
where new driving license seeker must attend this programme as a part of the driving licence issuing 
process.
Analytical Approach
The study employs a Diﬀerence-in-Diﬀerences (DiD) methodology to assess the impact of the WSOTR 
program on the behaviour of license applicants with respect to drinking and driving. This approach 
involves capturing behavioral responses of applicants before viewing the documentary and reassessing 
the same individuals after exposure. The observed change in behavior is attributed to the inﬂuence of the 
documentary.
Objective: To inﬂuence participants’ behavior (drivers, motorists and other road users) and promote 
responsible driving.
Output: The programme has been implemented across 87 RTOs in 12 states and UTs with 3,50,000+ 
beneﬁciaries.

energy generation, including solar installations and steam turbines, along with procurement of International Renewable Electricity 
Certiﬁcates (I RECs).

automation, and use of energy eﬃcient equipment have resulted in annual energy savings of approximately 1803 MWh.

continues to demonstrate leadership in energy conservation while advancing its long term decarbonization and sustainability objectives.

Indian Economy
India continued to demonstrate strong macroeconomic momentum 
during FY 2025-26, supported by resilient domestic consumption, 
sustained public expenditure, and a gradual recovery in private sector 
investments. India’s GDP grew by 7.7% in FY 2025–26, compared 
to 7.1% in the previous year, as per the Ministry of Statistics and 
Programme Implementation (MoSPI), reinforcing India’s position as 
one of the fastest growing major economies globally. 
On the external front, India advanced its trade engagement through 
agreements with key partners including the United Kingdom, the United 
States and the European Union, aimed at enhancing market access 
and strengthening trade linkages. These agreements are at various 
stages of engagement. 
In particular, India-UK FTA was a landmark one, aimed at reducing 
tariﬀs, expanding market access and deepening economic cooperation.
While global uncertainties and tariﬀ-related pressures moderated export 
momentum during the year, domestic demand remained the primary 
driver of growth. Policy focus remained on improving the ease of doing 
business through GST rationalisation and simpliﬁcation of compliance 
frameworks, supporting a more eﬃcient operating environment. 
Monetary policy also remained supportive, with the Reserve Bank of 
India reducing the repo rate by 100 basis points in FY 2025-26 to 5.25%, 
supporting growth and easing liquidity conditions.
Looking ahead, India’s growth trajectory remains structurally strong, 
led by domestic consumption and supported by ongoing reforms. 
This provides a favourable backdrop for discretionary consumption 
categories, including premium and prestige segments within the 
alcoholic beverages industry.

Regulatory Scenario in the Indian Market
India’s alcoholic beverage industry operates within a highly 
decentralised regulatory framework, in which state governments 
have authority over licensing, taxation, the legal drinking age and 
retail distribution. This system creates a fragmented environment, as 
compliance requirements, fees and procedures diﬀer across regions, 
posing operational challenges for companies that operate nationwide. 
In August 2025, the state of Maharashtra announced a revised 
liquor policy introducing a new low-tax category for grain-based 
spirits manufactured within the state under the Maharashtra Made 
Liquor (MML) framework. Eligibility for the category is linked to local 
manufacturing and ownership criteria, limiting participation by several 
national and foreign-invested spirits manufacturers operating outside 
Maharashtra, despite competing in similar consumer segments across 
the country.
The newly created category operates at highly attractive consumer 
price points, creating a signiﬁcant market distortion for national players. 
The policy has disrupted competitive parity, narrowed consumer choice, 
and added complexity to production and supply-chain planning for 
manufacturers with interstate operating models. Over time, such 
structural asymmetries could also discourage broader industry 
investment and undermine the principle of a level playing ﬁeld within 
the Indian alcobev sector.
In April 2026, the southern state of Karnataka introduced a landmark 
excise policy reform. As part of the overhaul, the state transitioned to 
an Alcohol-in-Beverage (AIB) based taxation structure, levying duties 
on actual alcohol content rather than total volume. The policy further 
removed state-administered retail price controls, enabling producers 
to determine pricing based on market considerations. The state 
also reduced excise slabs from 16 to 8 for alcobev products, thereby 
providing greater pricing ﬂexibility to manufacturers. Notably, taxes at 
the higher end of the spectrum were rationalised, making premium 
products more accessible to consumers and creating a meaningful 
segway for premiumisation in one of India’s largest alcobev markets. 
This structural simpliﬁcation of the excise framework has the potential 
to expedite premiumisation trends in the state, auguring well for the 
industry’s long-term growth trajectory.
Taxation remains a major component of the sector’s regulatory 
landscape, with excise duties, value-added tax and additional 
surcharges contributing to relatively high retail prices. Further restrictions 
on accessibility, advertising and consumption, including dry days and 
state-speciﬁc prohibitions, create additional variation in market access. 
In addition, every year several states revise the regulatory framework 
for alcoholic beverages. 
The India–UK Free Trade Agreement, expected to come into force soon, 
presents a signiﬁcant opportunity for premiumisation within the Indian 
alcoholic beverages industry. The agreement reduces import duties on 
Scotch whisky and gin from 150% to 75%, with a phased reduction 
to 40% over the next decade. Given India’s position as one of the 
world’s largest whisky markets, the trade pact is expected to improve 
accessibility of Scotch for Indian consumers, accelerate premiumisation 
trends and support growth across the alcobev and hospitality sectors.

Opportunities & Threats
Opportunities 
1. 
Favourable Demographics
 
 India’s alcoholic beverages market is expected to exhibit 
robust growth as the rising number of young adults enter the 
legal drinking age. The addition of this large group of young 
adult consumers, coupled with increasing disposable incomes 
and evolving lifestyle preferences, is likely to boost demand 
across product categories. As more young adults of legal 
drinking age enter the market, their preferences are expected 
to inﬂuence consumption patterns, particularly in premium and 
aspirational segments. 
2. 
Premiumisation
 
 Rising aﬄuence and aspiration are accelerating the shift towards 
premium and super-premium alcoholic beverages, thereby 
creating opportunities for capturing the consumer opportunity 
through high-value product portfolio accretive to margins. 
3. 
Emergence of Craft and Niche Segments
 
 The rise of craft distilleries and small-batch producers is 
transforming the industry landscape. Innovative beverage 
formats, including ﬂavoured spirits, artisanal cocktails and 
experimental blends, are gaining popularity among urban 
consumers. Emerging categories, including craft spirits, ﬂavoured 
products and RTDs, are expanding consumption occasions and 
attracting new consumers.
4. 
Sustainability and Eco-friendly Packaging
 
 Growing consumer and business environmental awareness is 
driving the adoption of sustainable practices across the alcoholic 
beverages industry. Manufacturers are increasingly focusing on 
eco-friendly packaging solutions, such as recyclable glass bottles, 
lightweight materials and environmentally responsible production 
processes, to reduce their environmental footprint.
5. 
Modern Retail and Digital Growth
 
 The growth of organised retail and modern trade channels 
has improved the accessibility of products and market reach 
for alcoholic beverage brands. Premium retail outlets and 
specialised liquor stores are playing an increasingly important 
role in distribution. In addition, digital engagement and direct-
to-consumer communication platforms are helping companies 
strengthen customer relationships and enhance brand visibility.

6. 
Hospitality and Tourism-driven Consumption
 
 The growth of the hospitality and tourism sectors is expected 
to further support demand for alcoholic beverages. Premium 
bars, restaurants, hotels and nightlife venues are increasingly 
oﬀering curated beverage experiences, encouraging consumers 
to explore premium and innovative alcoholic products. Tourism-
driven destinations are also contributing to the nationwide growth 
of on-premise consumption. 
7. 
Evolving Social Norms driving Cultural Shift 
 
 The gradual decline in social stigma surrounding alcohol 
consumption, especially among younger adults and women, 
oﬀers a substantial opportunity for brands to broaden their 
target audience. This shift in cultural attitudes allows companies 
to develop and introduce products that align with changing social 
norms and evolving lifestyle preferences, catering to a more 
diverse and inclusive consumer base.
Constraints & Threats 
1. 
Fragmented and Complex Regulatory Environment:
 
 The highly decentralised regulatory framework – where each state 
governs its own excise, licensing and retail policies – remains a 
major challenge. This fragmentation increases compliance costs, 
complicates pan-India distribution strategies and raises barriers 
for scaling. Adverse policy movements are an ongoing risk for 
any alcobev business in India. 
2. 
High Taxation and Pricing Pressure:
 
 Multiple layers of excise duties, VAT and state surcharges 
signiﬁcantly inﬂate retail prices, which can constrain consumption 
growth, especially in price-sensitive segments. High taxation also 
makes premium and imported products less aﬀordable for broad 
consumer groups. 
3. 
Advertising Restrictions:
 
 Strict regulations on direct advertising – through mainstream 
media channels – limit brands’ ability to build awareness and 
engage consumers. This necessitates alternative marketing 
approaches, which are less eﬀective and often resource-intensive. 
4. 
Illicit Alcohol
 
 Unregulated alcohol continues to impact legitimate industry 
growth and consumer safety.
Company Overview
Diageo India, also known as United Spirits Ltd. (hereafter referred to 
as ‘USL’ or ‘the Company’), is one of India’s leading beverage alcohol 
manufacturers, recognised for its premium and diversiﬁed product 
portfolio. The Company operates as a subsidiary of Diageo plc, with 
majority Relay B.V. holding a majority ownership stake of approximately 
55.88% of the equity shareholding. USL, headquartered in Bengaluru, 
has established one of the largest manufacturing networks in the 
Indian alcoholic beverages industry, operating 34 production facilities 
across the country. The Company also maintains a robust distribution 
ecosystem covering more than 75,000 outlets, supporting wide product 
availability and eﬃcient market penetration.
USL places sustainability, responsible consumption and community 
development at the core of its operating philosophy. The Company 
integrates these principles into its business practices to ensure long-
term environmental stewardship, promote safe and responsible drinking 
and contribute positively to the communities in which it operates. 
The Company continues to prioritise continuous innovation, portfolio 
premiumisation and enhanced consumer engagement as central 
elements of its strategy to drive long-term growth. 
USL completed the acquisition of NAO Spirits on 26th June 2025, 
acquiring a controlling 97.07% stake. NAO Spirits, recognised for its 
award-winning gin brands Greater Than and Hapusa, will now operate 
as a subsidiary of USL. During FY 2025-26, USL increased its stake in V9 
Beverages Private Limited (‘Sober’), a producer of non-alcoholic spirit 
alternatives, raising its holding from 15% to 25% on a fully diluted basis. 
Product Portfolio 
The Company’s product portfolio is organised into three primary 
segments: Prestige & Above (P&A), Popular and Other. USL’s product 
portfolio comprises more than 50 brands across categories such as 
Scotch whisky, Indian-made foreign liquor (IMFL) whisky, malt, tequila, 
brandy, rum, vodka and gin. Key brands in the portfolio include 
Godawan, McDowell’s No. 1, Royal Challenge, Signature, Antiquity, 
Black Dog, Director’s Special Black, McDowell’s Rum, McDowell’s 
Brandy and McDowell’s X-Series. USL also distributes several 
international brands in India under licensing arrangements, including 
Don Julio, Singleton, Tanqueray, Captain Morgan, Johnnie Walker, 
J&B, Baileys, Lagavulin, Talisker, VAT 69, Black & White, Smirnoﬀ and 
Ciroc. During FY 2025–26, the Company achieved sales volumes of 
approximately 65 million cases, representing a 1.5% increase over the 
previous year. 
Operational and Financial Highlights 
In FY 2025-26, USL commenced a strategic review of its investment 
in Royal Challengers Sports Pvt Ltd (RCSPL), the company that owns 
the Indian Premier League (IPL) and Women’s Premier League teams, 
including the Royal Challengers Bengaluru franchise. Pursuant to the 
announcement dated March 24, 2026, RCSPL has been classiﬁed as 
discontinued operations. The transaction remains subject to approval 
from the Board of Control for Cricket in India, the Competition 
Commission of India (CCI) and other applicable regulatory authorities. 
Consequently, consolidated numbers do not include RCSPL, and prior 
year numbers have also been restated accordingly. 
Prestige & Above: During FY 2025-26, the Prestige & Above (P&A) 
segment contributed 89.6% of the Company’s net sales value, reﬂecting 
an increase of 1.1% compared to the same period in the previous year. 
Net sales in the P&A segment grew by 8.6% during this period. 
Popular: Meanwhile, the Popular segment accounted for 9.0% of net 
sales in FY 2025-26, a slight 0.7% decline from the prior year. Net sales 
in the Popular segment declined by 0.3% over the same period.

Business Outlook 
USL remains focused on navigating the evolving competitive and 
regulatory environment through its portfolio-led strategy, enabling agility 
in responding to changing market dynamics, regulatory developments 
and evolving consumer preferences while driving sustainable growth. 
The Company continues to strengthen commercial performance through 
sharper execution, targeted investments and a proactive competitive 
approach aimed at driving market share recovery. Consumer insights 
remain at the centre of planning and decision-making, enabling more 
focused portfolio, innovation and growth interventions.
USL continues to invest in high-potential growth areas through 
premiumisation, core brand renovation, enhanced consumer-led 
marketing execution and strengthening its on-premise presence. The 
Company is also sharpening focus on the core USL portfolio, while 
accelerating the luxury portfolio through elevated brand experiences. 
In parallel, USL is increasing its focus on the white spirits segment as 
consumer repertoires continue to expand and evolve.
Category participation and category creation through portfolio white 
spaces remain key focus areas, enabling USL to drive consumer 
recruitment, expand consumption occasions and shape evolving 
consumption trends across segments. The Company’s franchising 
approach in select segments is supporting improved capital eﬃciency, 
working capital optimisation and margin enhancement, while its strong 
productivity focus continues to enable healthy reinvestment behind 
brands, innovation and long-term growth opportunities. Backed by 
a strong brand portfolio and disciplined execution, USL remains well 
positioned to capture long-term growth opportunities in India’s evolving 
alcoholic beverages market.
Risk & Mitigation Strategies
The Company follows a proactive and comprehensive risk management 
approach, embedding internal controls, governance, and business 
integrity into day-to-day operations. A structured enterprise-wide 
framework enables identiﬁcation, assessment, prioritisation, and 
mitigation of risks across strategic, ﬁnancial, operational (including 
ESG), compliance, cybersecurity, and emerging areas. Oversight is 
provided by the Risk Management Committee of the Board, which 
deﬁnes risk assessment, reviews key exposures, and monitors the 
eﬀectiveness of mitigation strategies. Regular risk assessments and key 
risk indicators support timely identiﬁcation and response to evolving 
risks. Risks are evaluated across short, medium, and long term horizons 
and categorised based on severity to enable prioritised and agile 
response. The Company maintains a zero-tolerance approach towards 
risks impacting safety, product quality, and regulatory compliance, 
while continuously strengthening controls to enhance resilience and 
sustain long-term performance.

Human Resources
USL places strong emphasis on building a people-centric organisation 
by investing in talent development, employee engagement and 
sustainable workforce practices. The Company’s human capital strategy 
is designed to support long-term business success by strengthening 
organisational capabilities and creating a high-performance culture 
aligned with future business requirements. USL employed more 
than 2,000 permanent employees, including executive staﬀ and 
permanent workmen.
The Company recognises its employees as key contributors to long-
term value creation and remains committed to nurturing internal 
talent pipelines. USL achieved an internal talent suﬃciency level 
of 49% during FY 2025-26, reﬂecting its focus on promoting career 
growth and developing in-house leadership capabilities. Learning and 
development, succession planning and internal mobility strengthen 
capability building, while inclusion eﬀorts focus on representation, 
psychological safety and progressive workplace policies. Performance 
is managed through a structured framework, supported by holistic 
wellbeing programmes that cover physical, emotional, ﬁnancial and 
social needs. USL’s overall voluntary attrition rate stood at 12.7% in 
FY 2025-26 making us one of the leading organisations in employee 
retention in the CPG industry. The Company’s Equal Opportunity policy 
promotes diversity in gender, ethnicity, age, sexual orientation and 
disability representation within the workforce. Women represented 30% 
of USL’s executive workforce and 31% of leadership roles, reﬂecting 
steady progress toward gender balance across the organisation. The 
Company will continue to strengthen its human capital framework by 
investing in employee capability development, improving engagement 
initiatives and building an inclusive organisational culture that supports 
sustainable business growth and operational excellence.

Internal Controls Systems
The Company has established a robust internal ﬁnancial control 
framework commensurate with the size, scale, and complexity of 
its operations, aimed at ensuring reliability of ﬁnancial reporting 
and compliance with applicable laws and regulations. The control 
environment is supported by a structured programme of internal and 
external audits, along with periodic management reviews. Oversight 
is exercised by the Board and its Committees to monitor the adequacy 
and implementation of controls.
The framework is designed to promote orderly and eﬃcient conduct 
of business, safeguarding of assets, prevention and detection of 
frauds and errors, and accuracy and completeness of accounting 
records. Continuous monitoring of the control environment and timely 
remediation of identiﬁed gaps support improved operational eﬃciency 
and strengthened governance. The Company continues to strengthen 
its internal ﬁnancial control framework through ongoing monitoring, 
periodic reviews, and timely remediation of identiﬁed gaps. This 
disciplined approach supports robust governance, enhances risk 
management, and enables the organisation to operate eﬃciently while 
responding eﬀectively to evolving business and regulatory requirements.

4.4 Performance Evaluation
 
 Pursuant to the provisions of the Act and Regulation 34(3) read 
with Schedule V(C) (4)(d) of the Listing Regulations, the NRC 
has prescribed performance evaluation criteria for Independent 
Directors as well as for the Non-Independent Directors, the 
Committees, and the entire Board of Directors. Based on the above 
requirement, a formal and rigorous Board review is undertaken 
on an annual basis with a focus on improving the eﬀectiveness 
of the Board, its Committees and each individual Director.
 
 As part of the above exercise, the Board had engaged Egon 
Zehnder, a leadership advisory firm on Board matters, to 
conduct the Board evaluation for FY2025-26, which evaluated 
parameters including guidance/support to Management 
outside Board/Committee meetings, degree of fulﬁllment of 
key responsibilities, eﬀectiveness of meetings amongst others. 
The performance evaluation of Independent Directors was 
carried out by the entire Board, excluding the Director being 
evaluated and the performance evaluation of the Chairperson 
and the Non-Independent Directors was carried out by the 
Independent Directors. The evaluation methodology included 
a detailed questionnaire covering various aspects of Board 
and Committee eﬀectiveness, governance oversight, strategic 
guidance, composition, quality of discussions, time commitment, 
stakeholder engagement, succession planning and risk oversight. 
In addition, individual one-on-one discussions were conducted 
with each Director to obtain qualitative insights and candid 
feedback on the functioning of the Board and its Committees. 
All Directors participated in the evaluation process. The ﬁndings 
from the questionnaire and discussions were consolidated and 
presented to the Board, enabling meaningful deliberations on 
key strengths, areas for enhancement and priorities for continued 
improvement in Board eﬀectiveness.
 
 The Board evaluation exercise reaﬃrmed the Board’s strong 
governance framework, eﬀective oversight, and constructive 
engagement across the Board and its Committees. The evaluation 
also highlighted the Board’s successful navigation of leadership 
and governance transitions in recent years, ensuring continuity 
and stability. As the Company enters its next phase of growth, 
the evaluation identiﬁed opportunities to further enhance the 
Board’s eﬀectiveness and future readiness. Key areas of focus 
include strengthening succession planning, deepening oversight 
of digital transformation and AI-related developments, fostering 
more robust risk discussions, maintaining a proactive regulatory 
watch, and advancing ESG integration into strategic decision-
making. These initiatives will support a sharper strategic focus and 
continued enhancement of Board and Committee eﬀectiveness.
 
 The Board evaluation process was completed successfully during 
the ﬁnancial year and recommendations from the said evaluation 
were discussed with the Board, including individual feedback 
being provided to respective directors. Based on the outcome of 
the evaluation, the Board and Committees have agreed on an 
action plan to further improve the eﬀectiveness and functioning 
of the Board and Committees.

and education program for all employees. Our Code enables our 
employees to make the right choices and demonstrate the highest 
standards of integrity and ethical behavior. Our Code has also 
been extended to suppliers, contractors and its subsidiaries.

standards, covering areas such as Countering Corruption Policy

Management & Security, Data Privacy & Personal Information, 
Health Safety & Personal Security, Prevention of Sexual 
Harassment at Workplace, Dignity at Workplace and Employee

team on various aspects of the compliance programs, to set the

Committee is obtained on an annual basis. Further, the Audit 
Committee, on quarterly basis, reviews the details of the RPTs 
entered into by the Company pursuant to such omnibus approval. 
The Policy also ensures compliance with regulatory guidelines 
and promotes accountability while adhering to the corporate 
governance principles.

business and on arm’s length basis and there were no materially 
signiﬁcant related party transactions that may have potential 
conﬂict with interest of the Company at large.
